title: PewDiePie unveils ‘uncensored’ Ajax AI model built to run on home PCs — creator says OpenAI banned him twice over model distillation used to build his product
key_facts: YouTuber PewDiePie unveiled Ajax, an 'uncensored' AI model built to run on home PCs, in a new video.
Ajax is a fine-tuned Qwen3.5-9B model that powers Odysseus, his self-hosted AI workspace, as an always-on assistant for search, browsing, email and calendar.
He says OpenAI banned him twice while he was building it; one email he shows names 'distillation' (training one model on another's outputs) as the reason.
He says he wanted to 'distill just a little bit'; his account was reinstated once, and the second ban came after he ran the model again to create seed data.

To remove refusals he used the open-source Heretic tool for 'abliteration'; he says it is not designed to give dangerous, actionable instructions, on his lawyer's advice, but the article says it is unclear what the real limits are.
He plans two more days of reinforcement learning, then re-running the refusal-removal step, quantizing and benchmarking before the next version.
The article says OpenAI recently attributed a distillation campaign to actors linked to Moonshot AI; no OpenAI comment on PewDiePie is quoted.
quote_evidence: According to the OpenAI email he shows, one ban was explicitly for “distillation,” the practice of using one model’s outputs or reasoning to train another.
The page says its refusal has been removed for a “freer, less restricted AI experience” and asks users to use it responsibly.
He uses nuclear weapons as an example, but it’s unclear what the real limits might be.
why_it_matters_hint: A well-known creator ships a small home-run model with refusals removed, and the story raises questions about copying from big labs' models.
event_date: Not stated; video and article around 2 Oct 2026.
notes: Read from the main session's fetch (HTTP 200); page header/subscription boilerplate skipped. Everything rests on the creator's own video and the email he shows; no response from OpenAI is quoted.
